newsitem.title: USA: GM begins a second $2.5 billion stock buy-back plan.
newsitem.headline: GM begins a second $2.5 billion stock buy-back plan.

text.p: DETROIT, Aug 4 (Reuter) General Motors Corp., which just completed buying back $2.5 billion worth of its stock, said Monday that it began a second $2.5 billion share repurchase programme.

"Today's actions underscore our ongoing commitment to improve the investment value of GM stock," Chairman John F. Smith Jr. said in a statement. "We've been implementing a number of initiatives to promote this goal, including repurchase programmes."

Investors, however, sold off the stock, which had hit a 52-week high of $64.50 on Friday. GM shares lost $1.94 to $62.56 in heavy trading on the New York Stock Exchange, where they were among the most actively traded issues.
GM said it had bought back about 43.7 million shares of its common stock since January.
"We believe that stock repurchase programmes are a great way to return excess cash directly to stockholders," Smith said.

The company said its latest stock repurchases will be made over a 12-month period, principally through open market transactions, and would represent 5 percent of the outstanding shares of GM $1-2/3 common stock.
The GM board also declared quarterly dividends on GM's common stock, unchanged from the previous quarter.

"We'll continue to review the dividend rate quarterly, keeping in mind that our priority here is to provide GM stockholders with a competitive dividend that is sustainable throughout the business cycle," Smith said.

The quarterly dividend on GM $1-2/3 par value common stock is 50 cents a share; the dividend on GM Class H common stock is 25 cents a share. Each dividend is payable Sept. 10, 1997, to holders of record on Aug. 14, 1997.
The company said the number of GM $1-2/3 common shares outstanding at the end of June was 721.4 million, down from 756 million shares at the end of 1996.
The 4.6 percent reduction was the result of the stock repurchased by GM since January, the company said.
